headline: Union Minister of State for Rural Development Dr. Pemmasani Chandrasekhar Reviews Progress of DDU-GKY 2.0, Calls for Timely Implementation and Digital Reforms
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

Union Minister of State for Rural Development Dr. Pemmasani Chandrasekhar Reviews Progress of DDU-GKY 2.0, Calls for Timely Implementation and Digital Reforms

Government Accelerates DDU-GKY 2.0 Implementation with New Digital Initiatives and Citizen-Centric Reforms

04 AUG 2026 7:45PM by PIB Delhi

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is one of the cluster of initiatives under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through placement linked skilling programs.

A review meeting on the implementation of the DDU-GKY was held today i.e. 04.08.2026 at Sanchar Bhawan under the Chairmanship of Shri Pemmasani Chandrasekhar, Hon'ble Minister of State for Rural Development and Communication.

The meeting was attended by Ms. M.G. Jayasree, Joint Secretary (Rural Skills-II), Shri Santosh K Tiwari, Director (Skills), Ms. Deepika Aggarwal, Dy. Director, NIC and other senior officials.

headline: CAQM extends Monitoring and Enforcement of Dust Mitigation measures across NCR; More ULBs empowered to Prosecute Gross Violators at C&D Sites
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

CAQM extends Monitoring and Enforcement of Dust Mitigation measures across NCR; More ULBs empowered to Prosecute Gross Violators at C&D Sites

04 AUG 2026 7:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has issued an amendment dated 03.08.2026 to its Statutory Direction No. 86 to further strengthen enforcement against violations of dust mitigation measures at Construction and Demolition (C&D) sites with plot area less than 500 sqm. across the National Capital Region (NCR).

The amendment widens the ambit of enforcement by extending the powers to initiate prosecution against gross violators to additional Municipal Corporations, Development Authorities, Municipal Councils, Municipal Boards and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) in the NCR.

Statutory Direction No. 86, issued on 02.01.2025 and amended on 24.06.2025, had authorised the Commissioner/Zonal Deputy Commissioners of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), Secretary, New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC), and Commissioners/Chief Executives/Deputy Commissioners of various ULBs in Gurugram, Faridabad, NOIDA, Greater NOIDA, Ghaziabad and Sonipat to file a complaint/prosecution before the jurisdictional Judicial Magistrate in cases of gross violations of directions/orders relating to dust and air pollution control and mitigation measures at such sites within their respective jurisdictions.

The Direction also empowered these authorities to order closure of such sites and impose or realise Environmental Compensation (EC) in cases of gross violations, including those relating to the GRAP Schedule in respect of C&D activities.

Recognising that a significant number of construction projects on plots having an area of less than 500 sqm. are also ongoing in several other Municipal Corporations and bigger cities/towns in the NCR, which contribute significantly to the overall PM10 and PM2.5 load attributed to the C&D sector, the Commission has expanded the enforcement framework to ensure more effective implementation of dust mitigation measures across the region.

Accordingly, the powers to initiate prosecution against gross violators of dust mitigation measures at C&D sites have now been extended to additional Municipal Corporations, Development Authorities and Urban Local Bodies across the NCR, including Manesar, Karnal, Panipat, Rohtak, Meerut, Alwar, Bharatpur, Bhiwadi and Neemrana, besides strengthening the existing enforcement mechanism in the NCR.

The amended Direction also requires all concerned agencies to submit a monthly status report to the Commission on complaints and prosecutions filed, along with the monthly progress reports already being submitted. This reporting mechanism is expected to strengthen accountability and facilitate closer monitoring of enforcement actions across the NCR.

During the last quarter, April–June 2026, 16,195 inspections were undertaken by DPCC/SPCBs at C&D sites in Delhi, 909 sites in Haryana (NCR), 230 sites in Uttar Pradesh (NCR) and 160 sites in the NCR districts of Rajasthan.

Considering the large number of C&D activities being undertaken across the NCR, particularly smaller construction projects on plots measuring less than 500 sqm., expanding the enforcement framework to additional Municipal Corporations, Development Authorities, Municipal Councils, Municipal Boards and ULBs assumes considerable significance for ensuring effective implementation of dust mitigation measures and strengthening compliance across the region.

The Commission has reiterated that effective enforcement of dust control measures at C&D sites remains a vital component of improving the overall air quality of the region. The expanded enforcement mechanism shall ensure stricter compliance, strengthen deterrence against violations and contribute significantly towards reduction of dust emissions across the NCR.

04 AUG 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Education today opened the online registration portal for Yuva Sangam Phase VII under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB) initiative. Interested youth aged 18–30 years, including students of Higher Education Institutions, NSS/NYKS volunteers, and young professionals, are eligible to register through the official portal at https://ebsb.aicte-india.org

The last date of registration for Yuva Sangam Phase VII is Aug 18, 2026.

For Yuva Sangam Phase VII, 20 Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), that is, IITs, IIMs, Central Universities and NITs have been identified as nodal institutions to host and facilitate the exchange programme. Selected participants will undertake five to seven day educational and cultural tours (excluding travel days) to their paired States/UTs, where they will gain firsthand exposure to local traditions, educational institutions, governance initiatives, innovation ecosystems, industries, heritage sites, and community life.

The Ministry of Education encourages youth from across the country to seize this unique opportunity to experience India's vibrant diversity, interact with peers from different regions, and become ambassadors of the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat vision.

headline: BRICS-TCA Symposium and JMC Meeting Convenes under the Guidance of MSDE, Government of India
fullText:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

BRICS-TCA Symposium and JMC Meeting Convenes under the Guidance of MSDE, Government of India

Two-day BRICS-TCA meeting examined digital, green and demographic shifts affecting skills and workforce needs

India placed proposals for a BRICS International Skill Gap Study, BRICS Skills Competition and Compendium of Good Practices before the JMC

04 AUG 2026 7:10PM by PIB Delhi

The BRICS Technical and Vocational Education and Training Cooperation Alliance (BRICS-TCA) Research Symposium and Joint Management Committee (JMC) Meeting was held during August 3 - 4, 2026, at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi.

The event was held under the theme "Sustainable and Digitally Enabled TVET: The BRICS Perspective", the two-day meeting brought together representatives from BRICS countries, international organisations, academia, industry and training institutions. The event was convened by National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), under the guidance of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), Government of India.

Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, said, “Skills are no longer merely a social intervention; they are critical economic infrastructure that shapes productivity, industrial competitiveness and workforce resilience. As BRICS nations, representing over 40 per cent of the world’s population, we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to build agile, inclusive and future-ready skilling systems. Through deeper cooperation in labour-market intelligence, institutional strengthening, joint research and emerging areas such as AI and green technologies, BRICS-TCA can help translate our collective demographic strength into shared prosperity and a more resilient global workforce.”

Shri. Anandrao V. Patil, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Education, emphasised lifelong learning, stating, “A degree can no longer mark the end of learning. Education systems must allow learners to move flexibly between classrooms, workplaces and digital platforms throughout their lives. India’s National Education Policy 2020 supports this through multidisciplinary education, credit portability and the integration of vocational and higher education. BRICS cooperation can carry this forward through joint curricula, institutional exchanges and wider recognition of qualifications and micro-credentials.”

Shri. Rajiv Bodwade, Joint Secretary (MER-III), Ministry of External Affairs, underscored the importance of skill diplomacy, stating, “Under India’s BRICS Chairship, skills cooperation must translate our shared demographic and economic strengths into practical, people-centric outcomes. A stronger focus on skills diplomacy can support orderly mobility, credible certification and closer institutional coordination across member countries. India remains ready to share its experience in migration partnerships, digital skilling platforms and transparent mobility systems to advance secure and mutually beneficial workforce pathways across the Global South.”

Shri. Arunkumar Pillai, Chief Executive Officer, NSDC, and Rotating Chair, BRICS-TCA, highlighted the need for practical cooperation, stating, “BRICS is navigating three transitions at once: digital, green and demographic. By 2030, 86 per cent of employers expect AI and information-processing technologies to transform business, while 39 per cent of workers’ core skills are likely to change. Renewable energy already supports 16.6 million jobs globally. At the same time, some member countries have expanding young workforces, while others face structural labour shortages. The opportunity is significant, but the real challenge is trust and recognition across skills systems. Comparable qualifications, verifiable digital credentials and common standards can turn this demographic strength into mobility, opportunity and shared growth.”

The inaugural session was chaired by Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Shri. Dilip Kumar, Director General, Directorate General of Training; Shri. Anandrao V. Patil, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Education; Shri. Niranjan Kumar Sudhansu, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Smt. Manisha Sensarma, Senior Economic Advisor, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Shri. Rajiv Bodwade, Joint Secretary (MER-III), Ministry of External Affairs; and Shri. Arunkumar Pillai, Rotating Chair, BRICS-TCA and Chief Executive Officer, National Skill Development Corporation.

The inaugural session was followed by a plenary session where the BRICS member countries such as Brazil, Russia, China, UAE, Iran and India presented their country's flagship initiatives on vocational education and skill development. After the plenary session, there were two panel discussions, on ‘Green Skills Development and Financing Mechanisms for Sustainability Initiatives’ and ‘Digital Transformation and AI, VR and AR for TVET’.

The Joint Management Committee (JMC) meeting on August 4 considered the synopsis of deliberations of the Research Symposium and received input from member countries on future priorities. Under India’s Chairship, three proposals were discussed. First, a framework of international skill gap study for BRICS was discussed to identify the gaps in emerging occupations and workforce shortages; second, a BRICS skills competition will be conducted to promote vocational excellence and a shared understanding of competence; and third, a compendium of good practices in TVET will be developed covering industry partnerships, digital learning, qualifications, and financing mechanism.

Representatives from the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, the World Bank, International Labour Organization, UNESCO, Universities and industry including Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), also participated in the deliberations.

headline: Strengthening Rural Agriculture Through Modern Cold Storage: How VCF-SC Enabled Meenakshidevi Hi-Tech Agro Industry Pvt. Ltd. to Empower Farmers and Create Sustainable Livelihoods

04 AUG 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

Agriculture is the backbone of India's rural economy, but inadequate post-harvest infrastructure often results in significant losses for farmers and limits their income. Modern cold storage facilities play a crucial role in preserving agricultural produce, improving its quality and extending its shelf life, thereby ensuring better market value for farmers. Demonstrating how timely institutional support can transform rural enterprises, Meenakshidevi Hi-Tech Agro Industry Pvt. Ltd., promoted by Ms. A. Amutha Devi, has emerged as an important contributor to agricultural infrastructure in Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, through the establishment of a modern cold storage facility.

Recognising the project's potential to strengthen the agricultural value chain and generate rural employment, the Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment extended financial assistance of ₹4.95 crore in 2017 through Venture Capital assistance comprising Equity and Optionally Convertible Debentures. The financial support enabled the company to establish a 5,000 MTPA cold storage unit consisting of five chambers of 1,000 MT each, significantly enhancing post-harvest storage capacity in the region.

Modern Cold Storage Infrastructure for Agricultural Growth

The project has enabled the optimum utilisation of resources while ensuring better quality and longer shelf life of agricultural produce. By providing reliable storage infrastructure, the enterprise has empowered farmers to secure remunerative prices for their produce instead of resorting to distress sales. headline: Government Strengthens Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme to Boost Higher Education Among Scheduled Caste Students
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

Government Strengthens Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme to Boost Higher Education Among Scheduled Caste Students

Revised Funding Pattern, Direct Benefit Transfer and End-to-End Online Processing Ensure Greater Transparency and Timely Scholarship Delivery

04 AUG 2026 7:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government is implementing the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) Scheme for Scheduled Caste (SC) students with the objective of significantly increasing the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of SC students in higher education, particularly those belonging to the poorest households. The scheme provides financial assistance at the post-matriculation and post-secondary levels, enabling eligible Scheduled Caste students to pursue and complete their education.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply to Shri Golla Baburao in Rajya Sabha, informed the House that the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme has been implemented continuously in the State of Andhra Pradesh since 2020-21. Scholarships have been disbursed to eligible applicants across all districts of the State.

According to the latest available data, Andhra Pradesh received Central Assistance of ₹149.03 crore, benefiting 81,667 students during 2026-27 (up to 24 July 2026).

The Minister further informed that the funding pattern of the scheme was revised in 2020-21, replacing the earlier concept of State Committed Liability with a fixed Centre-State sharing ratio of 60:40, while the ratio for North-Eastern States has been fixed at 90:10. The revised funding pattern has reduced the financial burden on States and enhanced the Central Government's contribution towards the scheme.

The House was also informed that several transformative reforms have been introduced under the scheme to improve efficiency, transparency and accountability. These include end-to-end online processing of applications, digital verification of eligibility through linkage with available databases, faster verification, continuous monitoring, prevention of duplication and timely delivery of scholarship benefits.

Further, the Government introduced Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) under the scheme from 2021-22, ensuring that scholarship amounts are transferred directly into the Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of eligible students. The initiative has simplified the flow of funds, improved transparency and ensured accurate targeting of beneficiaries. Applications are invited through the designated State scholarship portals or the National Scholarship Portal, while the release of the Central share is contingent upon the timely release of the corresponding State share.

The Minister also informed that delays in verification of applications by States and delays in the release of the State share can consequently delay the release of the Central assistance to eligible beneficiaries. The Government continues to work with States and Union Territories to ensure timely verification and disbursement of scholarships so that eligible Scheduled Caste students receive financial assistance without delay.

The Central Government is implementing the Post-Matric Scholarship (PMS) for Scheduled Castes and Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes & Others as Centrally Sponsored Schemes to promote educational empowerment of Scheduled Caste students across the country. The schemes are implemented through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode, ensuring timely, transparent and efficient disbursement of scholarship benefits to eligible students.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale shared these details in a written reply to Shri Kota Srinivasa Poojary, Shri Tejasvi Sury, Shri Jaswantsinh Sumanbhai Bhabhor, Shri Pradeep Kumar Singh, Shri Bharatsinhji Shankarji Dabhi, Shri Yogender Chandolia, Smt. Meeting to Deliberate on Key Priorities Including ECCE, Skill Development, Research and Innovation, Mutual Recognition of Qualifications and Academic Leadership

04 AUG 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Education, under India’s BRICS chairship 2026, is scheduled to host the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting and the 3rd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meeting from August 5–7, 2026 in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. These meetings would bring together education ministers, senior officials and delegates from BRICS member countries to discuss topics of collaboration, including the following priority areas:

(a) Strengthening Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE);

(b) Strengthening skill development and enhanced cooperation under the BRICS TVET Cooperation Alliance (TCA);

(c) Promoting collaborative research, innovation and start-ups;

(d) Strengthening Mutual Recognition of Qualifications (MRQ); and

(e) Capacity building for academic leadership.

India’s BRICS chairship is guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability”, reflecting the people-centric and humanity-first approach articulated by the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, at the 2025 BRICS Summit in Rio de Janeiro.

The 13th Education Ministers’ Meeting and the 3rd Senior Officials’ Meetings would build upon a series of engagements held under the BRICS Education Track during India’s chairship. The 1st and 2nd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meetings were held earlier on 7th and 28th April 2026, respectively, followed by the BRICS Network University Conference and International Governing Board Meeting on July 20 –21, 2026. The previous engagements have helped shaped discussions and build consensus on the priority areas and proposed outcomes for the Ministerial Meeting.

Ahead of the 13th Education Ministers’ Meeting, the BRICS TVET Symposium and the Joint Management Committee (JMC) meeting of the BRICS TVET Cooperation Alliance were also held in New Delhi on August 3–4, 2026, led by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. These engagements seek to deepen cooperation among BRICS countries in technical and vocational education and training, skills development and workforce preparedness and to consolidate and exchange research and best practices across the priority themes.

Alongside these high-level inter-governmental engagements, India’s BRICS chairship is placing strong emphasis on youth participation and people-to-people exchanges. In this spirit, Model BRICS has been conceptualised as a student-focused initiative to be organised on the sidelines of BRICS Ministerial Meetings across India. The initiative seeks to familiarise young citizens with BRICS processes while strengthening their understanding of diplomacy, multilateral cooperation and consensus-building.

fullText:

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has not formulated any separate phased national policy to incentivize flex-fuel vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than 20% ethanol

04 AUG 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi

Production Linked Incentive scheme for Automobile & Auto Components (PLI-Auto scheme) is implemented on an all-India basis. The current status of implementation of PLI-Auto scheme is as below:-

Parameter | Cumulative till 31.03.2026

To boost domestic manufacturing and localisation of AAT products, PLI-Auto scheme mandates minimum Domestic Value Addition (DVA) of 50% for availing incentives. As on 28.07.2026, 18 applicants have received DVA certificates for 155 AAT products/variants.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has not formulated any separate phased national policy to incentivize flex-fuel vehicles operating on fuel blended with more than 20% ethanol.

MHI has not conducted any study regarding incentivization of flex-fuel and electric vehicles.

The government has adopted a balanced approach to the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme, ensuring that water sustainability, food security and farmers' interests remain paramount. Under the National Policy on Biofuels, ethanol is produced from multiple approved feedstocks, including sugarcane-based feedstocks, maize, damaged foodgrains, broken rice, foodgrains unfit for human consumption, surplus foodgrains approved by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee (NBCC) and other approved agricultural feedstocks.

The government is also promoting crop diversification towards comparatively less water-intensive feedstocks such as maize. An Expert Committee constituted by Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare in 2024 examined the water requirement of various ethanol feedstock crops & its recommendations are being considered while implementing the programme.

Water-use efficiency is also being enhanced through micro-irrigation, drip irrigation and other water conservation measures under the Per Drop More Crop component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana. Many sugar mills are also encouraging farmers to adopt water-efficient cultivation practices.

Molasses-based distilleries with incineration boilers and grain-based distilleries are required to operate as Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) units, enabling recycling and reuse of process water while eliminating liquid effluent discharge.

headline: An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis
fullText:
Ministry of Heavy Industries

An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis

04 AUG 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi

The PM E-DRIVE Scheme is being implemented on a pan-India basis, and no State-wise allocation of funds has been made. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 42,035 EVs have been sold in Assam, under this Scheme which includes 8,003 EVs sold in Cachar district. Further, a total of 40,009 EVs have been incentivised in Assam with a total reimbursement of ₹ 99.10 crore to OEMs.

An allocation of ₹2,000 crore has been made under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme for deployment of Electric Vehicle Public Charging Stations (EVPCS) on pan India basis including the state of Assam. Assam has not yet submitted any proposal for deployment of EVPCS under the PM E-DRIVE scheme.

No such assessment has been done by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) for Cachar district of Assam.

The MHI is implementing following schemes to promote electric mobility, strengthen charging infrastructure and encourage the adoption of electric public transport and commercial vehicles across the country including Cachar district and other parts of Assam:

Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) Scheme Phase-II: The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme provided demand incentive for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting up of EV public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws. In addition, 5,297 electric buses (e-buses) have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country.

Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore.

Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage : The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries.

PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore is implemented from 01.04.2024. This scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging stations (EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e-buses out of which 13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e-buses have been approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for deployment of EV Public Charging Stations on pan India basis.

PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme: This Scheme notified on 28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e-bus operators in case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs).

Following initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to increase the use of electric vehicles in the country: –

i. GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been reduced to 5%.

ii. The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery-operated vehicles will be given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements.

iii. MoRTH issued an advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help reduce the initial cost of EVs.

headline: PREVENTION OF SOIL DEGRADATION
fullText:
Ministry of Agriculture &

PREVENTION OF SOIL DEGRADATION

04 AUG 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi

The Government has taken various measures to prevent soil degradation and promote judicious use of fertilizers, manures and herbicides by the farmers as follows-

Balanced use of fertilizer is promoted under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, being implemented since 2014-15. Under the scheme, Soil Health Cards (SHCs) are generated which provide nutrient status of soil, based on which crop-wise fertilizer recommendations are provided to farmers, thereby promoting balanced and efficient nutrient management. SHC helps in enhancing crop productivity, reduce cultivation costs, and promote sustainable agriculture. So far, 26.09 crore Soil Health Cards have been generated and issued to farmers. 130627 farmer’s trainings, 7.17 lakh demonstrations, 7425 farmer’s Melas/ campaigns on soil health card recommendations have been organized across the country.

National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 25 November 2024. NMNF promotes chemical-free, nature-based farming practices using on-farm inputs. Under the scheme, 23.13 lakh farmers have been registered and 11.44 lakh hectares area have been covered, Government has adopted Integrated Pest Management (IPM) as cardinal principle and main plank of plant protection in the overall Crop Production Programme since 1985. IPM is an eco-friendly approach which encompasses cultural, mechanical, biological and need based chemical control measures. The Integrated Pest Management-cum-Locust Division of Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage (DPPQ&S) promotes Integrated Pest Management (IPM) through its 48 Central Integrated Pest Management Centres (CIPMCs) and Locust-cum-CIPMCs located across 28 States and 2 UTs. Farmers are trained through Farmer Field Schools (FFS), 2-day HRD programmes, and safe & judicious use of pesticides awareness programmes. These programmes enable farmers to integrate cultural, mechanical and biological control measures.

Special awareness Campaign and Khet Bachao Abhiyan on balanced use of fertilizers have been conducted by Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) and ICAR during the current Kharif Season 2026 wherein total 2,94,554 programs covering 1,36,73,465 farmers have been achieved. During the campaign, farmers have also been made aware on Natural/Organic Farming, bio-inputs, alternative fertilizers etc.

Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is implemented since 2015-16. PKVY promotes organic farming by providing end-to-end support covering production, processing, certification, and marketing. So far, 18.93 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming and 33.63 lakh farmers have been benefited.

Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) is implemented since 2015-16 to promote organic farming in North Eastern States. So far, 2.36 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming and 2.74 lakh farmers have been benefited.

The Government also promotes Soil Organic Carbon Enhancer namely, Fermented Organic Manure (FOM) /Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM) as a part of judicious use of fertilizers. During 2024-25, the annual consumption of FOM/LFOM was 3.36 LMT. During the current Kharif Season (1.4.2026 to 16.7.2026), the consumption of FOM/LFOM is 11.86 LMT.

Indian Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) through Directorate of Weed Research, Jabalpur is promoting sustainable Integrated Weed Management (IWM) for judicious use of herbicides in different crops and cropping systems through research, demonstrations, capacity building and extension programmes. The Directorate disseminates scientific advisories through mobile-based services, social media, printed literature and village-level extension programmes to promote the efficient and environmentally safe use of herbicides. The Directorate is also analyzing the herbicide residues in soil and food chain, and accordingly suggesting farmers for crop management practices. These interventions have significantly contributed in reducing the indiscriminate use of herbicides thereby improving soil health and crop productivity.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

### OVERVIEW
The Government detailed a comprehensive suite of ongoing schemes and initiatives—including the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, National Mission on Natural Farming, Integrated Pest Management, and organic farming programs—aimed at preventing soil degradation and promoting the judicious use of fertilizers, manures, and herbicides, as presented in a written reply by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare in Lok Sabha on 4 August 2026.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Soil Health & Fertility Scheme (since 2014-15):** 26.09 crore Soil Health Cards generated and issued; 1,30,627 farmer trainings, 7.17 lakh demonstrations, and 7,425 farmer Melas/campaigns organized.
- **National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF):** Approved by Union Cabinet on 25 November 2024; 23.13 lakh farmers registered and 11.44 lakh hectares covered under chemical-free, nature-based farming.
- **Integrated Pest Management (IPM):** Adopted as cardinal principle since 1985; promoted through 48 Central Integrated Pest Management Centres (CIPMCs) and Locust-cum-CIPMCs across 28 States and 2 UTs; training via Farmer Field Schools, 2-day HRD programmes, and safe pesticide use awareness programmes.
- **Special Awareness Campaign & Khet Bachao Abhiyan (Kharif Season 2026):** 2,94,554 programs conducted covering 1,36,73,465 farmers; included awareness on natural/organic farming, bio-inputs, and alternative fertilizers.
- **Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) (since 2015-16):** 18.93 lakh hectares brought under organic farming; 33.63 lakh farmers benefited with end-to-end support for production, processing, certification, and marketing.
- **Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) (since 2015-16):** 2.36 lakh hectares under organic farming; 2.74 lakh farmers benefited in North Eastern States.
- **Fermented Organic Manure (FOM)/Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM) Consumption:** 3.36 LMT consumed during 2024-25; 11.86 LMT consumed during current Kharif Season (1 April 2026 to 16 July 2026).
- **Integrated Weed Management (IWM) by ICAR-Directorate of Weed Research, Jabalpur:** Promotes judicious herbicide use through research, demonstrations, capacity building, and extension; disseminates advisories via mobile services, social media, printed literature, and village-level programmes; conducts herbicide residue analysis in soil and food chain to guide crop management practices.
- **Source:** Information provided by Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Ramnath Thakur, in a written reply in Lok Sabha on 4 August 2026 (Release ID: 2294460).
